title: Tell Your Leader When Youre About to Disagree With Them
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article recommends a specific tactic for disagreeing productively with a leader: previewing that a disagreement is coming before actually stating it. It argues this small courtesy gives leaders — especially less secure ones, and especially in group settings — a moment to mentally prepare rather than feeling ambushed. The piece frames this preview not as weakness or hedging but as a relationally sensitive behavior that leaders consistently appreciate and respond to more favorably than an unannounced challenge.
points: Weak leaders resent unexpected disagreement, while strong leaders welcome candor but still dislike being surprised by it.
Previewing an upcoming disagreement gives a leader a moment to mentally prepare before hearing the substance.
This preview matters most in group settings, where less secure leaders are especially sensitive to public disagreement.
The preview lets the leader decide how forcefully to defend their position or how much to simply listen.
Leaders consistently view this small act of forewarning as supportive and relationally considerate.
quotes: Weak leaders have a difficult time when a team member has the “audacity” to disagree with them.
But, weak or strong, leaders don’t like to be surprised by disagreement from a team member or colleague.
The most effective team members forecast when they are about to disagree with their leader before making the details of their opposition known.
Less secure leaders are particularly face-sensitive to disagreement about their positions in the presence of others.
Leaders appreciate this advanced notification and think more highly of those who do it.
